t: Cassander founded the city around 315 BCE, the Romans made it a provincial capital on the Via Egnatia, and under Galerius and later emperors it became the second city of the Byzantine world after Constantinople.
The Ottomans took it in 1430, and after 1492 Sephardic Jews from Spain settled there, so that by 1519 they made up 54% of the city's population.
Greece took the city in 1912, the fire of 1917 destroyed its centre, the exchange of populations changed its makeup, and the deportation of 1943 destroyed its Jewish community.
dyk: In 1519, according to Ottoman archives, Thessaloniki had 15,715 Jews, 6,870 Muslims and about 6,635 Christians, and the Jews were 54% of the city's population.
ev: Cassander founds the city and names it after his wife Thessalonike
St Demetrius becomes the patron saint of the city
A naval force led by Leo of Tripoli sacks the city
Sultan Murad II captures the city from the Venetians
Ottoman archives record a Jewish majority of 54%
The Ottoman garrison surrenders to the Greek army
A fire destroys most of the old centre and leaves 72,000 people homeless
The deportation of the city's Jews to Auschwitz begins

f.founded: Around 315 BCE by King Cassander of Macedon, on or near the site of the ancient town of Therma and 26 other local villages; he named it after his wife Thessalonike, a half-sister of Alexander the Great.
f.where: On the northern edge of the Thermaic Gulf, at the north-west corner of the Aegean Sea, bounded on the west by the delta of the Axios, in Central Macedonia, Greece.
f.known: A city on the Roman Via Egnatia; Galerius's palace, arch and mausoleum; St Demetrius; the second city of the Byzantine Empire; the home of Cyril and Methodius; the Zealots of 1342; the largest Sephardic Jewish community; the Young Turk Revolution of 1908; the Great Fire of 1917
f.today: Thessaloniki is the second-largest city of Greece and the capital of the region of Central Macedonia.
